title: Today / Morning Brief
markdown:
`openexecutive.api.routes.today` serves the morning brief — a one-screen, read-only view of what is happening across the org. It is the default landing surface (the Next.js root renders `<Briefing>`).

`GET /today` returns `TodayResponse` assembled by `_build_today()`, which is synchronous and caller-agnostic:

- **`departments`** — per-department goal health, rolling up each department's goal counts (`total`, `at_risk`, `off_track`) plus its awaiting-workflow count, and `attention_goals`: the actual off-track/at-risk goals (worst first, capped at 3) with `key_result`, `current`, `target`, and `status`, so the briefing's Department card shows *which* goal is off and how far without a click. Empty for healthy/inactive departments.
- **`people`** — an attention-ranked roster. Each person carries `awaiting_action` count, soonest SLA, a `status` (`on_leave` / `needs_reply` / `awaiting` / `clear`), reachability, `overdue`, a server `priority` sort key, and a cached one-line `insight`. Sorted by `(-priority, full_name)`.
- **`proposals`** — all unread alerts (workflow approvals, triage-classified inbound, Executive signals, flagged artifacts, and gated calendar bookings). Each carries `score`, `category` (`action` vs `monitoring`), `surfaced_reason` from `openexecutive.briefing.ranking`, and `decision_instance_id` (set only when the proposal is backed by a decision-ledger row — a calendar booking awaiting approval). The UI splits them into 'mine' vs 'across the team' using `caller_person_id`. For decision-backed proposals the card's Approve/Reject call the `/decisions` endpoints (which book or cancel the event server-side and clear the alert) instead of the ack-and-hand-off-to-chat flow — so meeting bookings are reviewed in the briefing itself rather than on a separate page.
- **`narrative`** — a per-viewer Executive-voice header synthesized by `synthesize_briefing_narrative`; the principal gets the whole-company scope, teammates a role-scoped one. In the web UI each bullet of this narrative is a click target: clicking one hands off to chat (the same `onContinue` path as the proposal cards) seeded to discuss that item. The Executive recognizes it because every chat turn now carries a `<briefing>` digest of open alerts (see Memory).
- **`in_flight`** / **`awaiting`** — upcoming Executive commitments and people we are waiting on.
- **`talent`** — the active executive-search pipeline, rolled up by `briefing.talent_digest.build_talent_brief_items`: one item per non-terminal engagement (FILLED/CANCELLED dropped) with role, department, status, candidate count, per-stage counts, and four attention signals — `offers_expiring_soon` (extended offers within 72h of `expires_at`, or past it with no decision recorded — computed straight from the offers table so a missed nudge can't make the briefing stale), `needs_screening` (leads), `offers_out` (offers), and `stalled_count` (active candidates not touched in ≥7 days). Items sort expiring → offers → stalled → leads → size. It renders as the briefing's **Executive search** card (one per search; click-to-discuss hands off to chat via the same `onContinue` path), feeds the narrative (an offer landing or a search going cold re-writes the header — the narrative cache hash folds a talent fingerprint), and the same digest's `format_talent_for_prompt` is appended to the chat `<briefing>` block so the Executive can discuss live searches by client or role. One rollup, shared by all four surfaces, so the card / header / chat never disagree. See the Talent section.

The route resolves the caller from `x-caller-email`, then attaches the viewer-scoped narrative in a `BackgroundTask` so the request never blocks on an LLM call. `GET /today/activity` returns the recent self-initiated action rail — merged from fired scheduled actions (DMs, follow-ups, nudges, cadences), logged decisions, saved advice, completed workflow runs (briefings/check-ins/research), kicked-off initiatives, resolved gated decisions, and raised alerts, so it reflects all of the Executive's activity rather than just dispatched messages. The Pulse page (`/memories`) polls it (limit 100) every ~20s so new events stream into the 'Recent activity' card, which scrolls internally at a fixed height instead of growing the page. The `morning_brief` workflow calls `_build_today()` directly to build the standalone DM (via a different, enumerated prompt). `GET /morning-brief` is a deprecated alias.

## Multi-client practice section

In multi-client practice mode (2+ client slots — see the Client Companies section), the response gains an additive `practice_clients` list: rollup cards for the **parked** clients (overdue follow-ups, awaiting replies, unread alerts, onboarding due soon, renewal countdowns), each stamped with the save point its data reflects. Single-company installs always receive an empty list and the UI renders nothing.
